text:
alex: Quick question about cache headers for prompt/prefix caching: what's the agreed header name and format for a cache hit marker? We need something that works for streaming and for both prefix-only and full-response hits. Example we currently see `x-cache-hit: true` in infra but it's inconsistent across layers.

maria: Short answer: pick a single header that is stable. Proposal: `x-rw-cache` with semicolon-delimited kv: `hit=1;key_ver=3;partial=0;reason=prefill` — compact and machine-parseable. Works for streaming (header sent early) and for postmortem parsing. Thoughts?

sam: Concern: backward compat with SDKs and our analytics pipeline. If we change format we need a migration plan. Could we instead use two headers: `x-rw-cache-hit: 1` and `x-rw-cache-meta: key_ver=3;partial=0` ? Easier to parse for downstream systems that only check hit presence.

maria: Yeah that is simpler for consumers that only check presence of hit. Also streaming clients can check `x-rw-cache-hit` before body.

raj: From ops side: invalidation system needs to include key version bump. We already have an invalidation webhook that expects `team_id, model, prefix_key, version`. Proposed semantics: bump `key_version` on any mutation that affects prefix equivalence. Invalidation endpoint example: `POST /v1/cache/invalidate` body: `{\n  "scope":"team",\n  "prefix":"user:123",\n  "model":"gpt-neo",\n  "key_version":4\n}`. We'll add audit log and idempotency token.

alex: For partial hits (prefix-only) what's the flag? Should `partial=1` indicate prefix hit and we streamed remainder? Need to be explicit.

maria: Yes: `partial=1` means cached prefix tokens were used but final output generated. `full=1` means whole response served from cache with no generation. Keep both mutually exclusive.

raj: Ops note: when invalidation occurs we should publish an event to internal topic `cache.invalidations.v2` with `{prefix, model, new_key_version, cause}` so replicas can reconcile. Use exponential backoff for eventual consistency.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled to roll this header change Tue 09:00 PDT under feature flag `cache_header_v2`. Will post deploy window and smoke tests.

sam: Action items: (1) Maria to open RFC with exact header names + parsing rules. (2) Raj to extend invalidation webhook + publish invalidation events. (3) Alex to add analytics parsers for new headers and validate streaming behavior in staging. Please tag me in PRs. :thumbsup: 

maria: I'll draft RFC today. Punting on kv hashing format until RFC. Ping @sam for analytics schema.

alex: thanks all, will wait for RFC. If no objections by EOD Monday we'll flip the feature flag in staging.

maria: small note: when streaming we must emit `x-rw-cache-hit` in the initial response headers (or via HTTP/2 initial headers) — streaming clients need that early.

raj: Confirmed we can set header at connection start for gRPC/http2 and for chunked HTTP we'll send via initial status headers. Ops will ensure LB doesn't strip it.

sam: Also add test case in SDKs to check both header styles and a parser that tolerates both numeric and boolean values for compatibility (`1`/`0` and `true`/`false`).

alex: Quick example snippets for RFC: 
```
# header style A (single header)
x-rw-cache: hit=1;key_ver=3;partial=0;reason=prefill

# header style B (split)
x-rw-cache-hit: 1
x-rw-cache-meta: key_ver=3;partial=0;reason=prefill
```

maria: we'll include parsing rules (case-insensitive keys, tolerate extra semicolons, ignore unknown keys) and a sample parser in Go/Python in the RFC.

alex: Filed follow-ups: #1234 PR for header parsing, #1235 webhook changes, #1236 SDK test. Closing thread for async updates, will reopen if needed.
